mainTopic: Moving water and שביתה; why רבי יהושע בן לוי ruled both like רבי יוחנן בן נורי and like the lenient view in עירוב; whether one-against-many matters in rabbinic law
overview: The גמרא finishes its discussion of rain that falls on יום טוב. It rejects the idea that the water did not yet exist, because then it would be נולד and forbidden. Instead it says that water in clouds, and in the ocean, is always moving, so it never acquires שביתה. A ברייתא supports this: flowing rivers and springs are like the feet of whoever draws from them. Then רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and he also says that the הלכה follows the lenient view in עירוב. The גמרא explains why both rulings were needed: the general rule limits us to his leniencies, and the specific ruling shows we follow a lone lenient view even against the majority. רבא asks why the number of sages should matter in a rabbinic law. Two challengers prove that it does matter: רבי relied on the lone רבי אלעזר only בשעת הדחק, and רבי יוחנן followed the lone רבי עקיבא in mourning only because of a special rule to be lenient in אבל.

steps.title: If the water was not yet formed, it would be forbidden as newly created
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the earlier suggestion that the rainwater did not yet exist in its present form before יום טוב. If that were true, the water would count as נולד and be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the more so they should be considered newly created, so they would be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It had said the rainwater was not yet 'real water' before יום טוב, so it could not have acquired שביתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the water only came into being on יום טוב, that solves the שביתה problem but creates a worse one. Something that came into being on יום טוב is נולד, which is a type of מוקצה, so nobody would be allowed to use the water at all. The answer creates a bigger problem than the one it solved.

keyTerms.meaning: something newly created on שבת or יום טוב, forbidden to handle

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying rainwater really is forbidden. It is showing that the previous answer leads to an impossible result, so that answer must be dropped.

phrases.english: All the more so they would be considered 'newly created,'
phrases.notes: This goes back to the idea that the water didn't yet exist in its current form.

phrases.english: so they would be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the previous answer (from the preceding text) that the water was not yet formed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that rainwater did not acquire שביתה because it was not yet formed before יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the water did not exist before יום טוב, it is נולד and forbidden. That is a worse result than the original problem.

steps.title: Water in the clouds is always moving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. Water in clouds is constantly moving, so it never settles in one place and never acquires שביתה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the water in the clouds is constantly moving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old answer and gives a better one. The water existed, but it was never at rest, so it never acquired a fixed location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer avoids the נולד problem, because the water did exist before יום טוב. It also avoids the שביתה problem, because something that never stops moving does not 'settle' in any place. So the water has no תחום of its own. It may go wherever the person who takes it may go, like his feet.

phrases.english: Rather: the water in the clouds is constantly moving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement answer (אלא): it changes why the water has no שביתה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The water had no שביתה because it did not yet exist, which would make it נולד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water existed, but because it was in constant motion it never acquired שביתה.

steps.title: The same answer solves the ocean question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the new answer also removes the earlier difficulty about the ocean. Ocean water is also always moving, so it too never acquires שביתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have arrived at this answer, the ocean should not be difficult for you either: water in the ocean is also constantly moving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that its new answer solves a second, earlier problem. The problem was that the clouds draw their water from the ocean, so maybe the water already settled there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא worried that the water had acquired שביתה in the ocean before rising into the clouds. The principle of constant motion applies to the ocean too. So the water never settled there either.

keyTerms.meaning: now that you have arrived at this answer
it should not be difficult for you

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this answer,
the ocean should also not be difficult for you,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier question about water drawn up from the ocean.

phrases.english: since the water in the ocean is also constantly moving,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the new answer to solve an earlier difficulty about the ocean.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extension of an existing principle to a second difficulty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The water may have acquired שביתה in the ocean before rising into the clouds.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ocean water is also always moving, so it never acquired שביתה there.

steps.title: A ברייתא: flowing water belongs to everyone's feet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support. Flowing rivers and springs have no fixed location, so they are like the feet of each person who draws from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: flowing rivers and gushing springs are like the feet of all people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up the idea that moving water never acquires שביתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Like the feet of all people' means the water may be carried only as far as the person who draws it may walk. The water has no limit of its own. This ruling rests on the same reason as the answer above: water that keeps flowing never settles. That supports applying the rule to clouds and oceans.

keyTerms.meaning: and it was taught in a ברייתא
like the feet of every person; it goes wherever the person who takes it may go

steps.whatToRemember: Water in constant motion (clouds, oceans, rivers, springs) never acquires שביתה. It takes on the תחום of whoever draws it, and it is not נולד.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a ברייתא: flowing rivers
and gushing springs
are like the feet of all people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source supporting the constant-motion principle.
steps.raayaObject: Moving water does not acquire שביתה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: flowing rivers and gushing springs are like the feet of all people.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. In the משנה, רבי יוחנן בן נורי ruled that someone who was asleep when שבת began still gets 2000 אמות in every direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: a ruling on the dispute in the משנה about a person who was asleep when שבת began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוחנן בן נורי held that ownerless objects, and a sleeping person, still acquire שביתה. So the sleeper gets 2000 אמות. The חכמים limited him to 4 אמות. This מימרא rules for the lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא in the משנה who gives the sleeper 2000 אמות

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a halachic ruling on the dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי: one who slept as שבת began still has 2000 אמות in every direction.

steps.title: Did you hear it explicitly or by inference?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי יעקב בר אידי whether he heard this ruling directly from רבי יהושע בן לוי, or worked it out from a more general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי יעקב בר אידי: did you hear it explicitly, or did you hear it by inference?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא checks how reliable the report is. A ruling stated outright is stronger than one worked out from a general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ruling came only by inference, it could be wrong. The general principle might not really apply to this specific case. So רבי זירא wants to know the source before relying on it.

keyTerms.meaning: from a general rule; by inference

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi:
Did you hear it explicitly
or did you hear it by inference?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ אוֹ מִכְּלָלָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how reliable the source of the ruling is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהושע בן לוי stated this ruling outright, or it was inferred from a broader principle.

steps.title: I heard it explicitly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי answers that he heard the ruling stated outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אידי confirms that the ruling is a direct quote, not his own conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ruling was stated explicitly, it does not depend on whether a general principle really covers this case. The ruling for רבי יוחנן בן נורי stands on its own.

phrases.english: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling was heard explicitly from רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: What general rule could it have been inferred from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what general rule רבי זירא had in mind when he raised the possibility of an inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the general rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move. It wants to identify the general principle that could have produced this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's question assumed there was some broader statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי that might include this case. The גמרא now asks which statement that was.

phrases.english: What is the general rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the general principle referred to in רבי זירא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which general statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי could have implied this ruling.

steps.title: The general rule: follow the lenient view in עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The general rule is רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement that the הלכה follows the lenient view in matters of עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהושע בן לוי said: the הלכה follows the words of the one who is lenient regarding עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the broad principle. Since רבי יוחנן בן נורי is the lenient view in a law of this מסכת, one might have inferred the ruling from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's position is the lenient one, since it gives the sleeper 2000 אמות instead of 4. The general rule 'follow the lenient view in עירוב' would therefore seem to cover it. That is why רבי זירא wanted to know whether the ruling was stated explicitly. A general rule may not automatically apply to every case.

keyTerms.meaning: the laws of עירוב (and related שבת boundary laws)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי ruled explicitly like רבי יוחנן בן נורי. He also has a general rule that the הלכה follows the lenient view in עירוב, and the ruling might otherwise have been inferred from it.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha follows the words of the one who is lenient regarding eruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הַמֵּיקֵל בְּעֵירוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by naming the general rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The general rule is 'the הלכה follows the lenient view in עירוב.'

steps.title: Why were both rulings needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע בן לוי stated both the specific ruling and the general rule, since one seems to cover the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need both statements?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the two rulings from Steps 5 and 9 side by side and asks why both were said. This question sets up רבי זירא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי is the lenient view about the sleeping person, so the general rule 'follow the lenient view in עירוב' already seems to give the same result. If so, the specific ruling looks extra. The גמרא assumes a great teacher does not repeat himself for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (a formula asking why something was said at all)
Why do I need two? (asks why a teaching seems to be doubled)

phrases.english: And why do I need two [statements]?!
phrases.notes: The two are: 'הלכה כרבי יוחנן בן נורי' and 'הלכה כדברי המיקל בעירוב'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once Step 9 shows there is also a general rule, the גמרא asks why both rulings exist.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does each ruling teach that the other does not?

steps.title: The general rule limits the specific ruling to leniencies
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains the general rule is needed. Without it, we might follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי even where his view is strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Both are needed. Had he taught us only that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, I would have thought this applies whether it leads to a leniency or a stringency. So he teaches us that the הלכה follows the lenient view in עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא shows why the general rule was needed. The specific ruling alone might make us follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי in all his rulings, even his strict ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same משנה, רבי יוחנן בן נורי gives a lenient ruling (a sleeping person gets 2000 אמות) and a strict one (ownerless objects are limited to 2000 אמות from their place). The general rule tells us we follow him only on the lenient side. This explains half of the 'why both' question.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed (both statements are necessary)
I would have said (a mistaken first assumption)
This teaches us (what the statement adds)
The laws that set and extend שבת boundaries (here, the laws of תחומין)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן בן נורי is always the lenient one. In the same משנה he is strict about ownerless objects. That is exactly why the general rule was needed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: They are [both] necessary,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי,
phrases.english: for if he had taught us [only] that the halakha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא בֵּין לְקוּלָּא וּבֵין לְחוּמְרָא,
phrases.english: I would have said: both for leniency and for stringency,
phrases.notes: The leniency is the case of the sleeping person; the stringency is the case of ownerless objects.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הַמֵּיקֵל בְּעֵירוּב.
phrases.english: so he teaches us: the halakha follows the lenient view in eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by showing what the general rule adds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The general rule limits the ruling for רבי יוחנן בן נורי to his lenient positions only.

steps.title: Then why not state only the general rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the general rule is so useful, why was the specific ruling needed at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him say only, 'The הלכה follows the lenient view in עירוב.' Why do I need 'The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the general rule is needed, but now asks why the specific ruling was also said. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא showed the general rule is needed, but that seems to make the specific ruling extra. The general rule alone would already lead us to follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי on the sleeping person, since he is lenient there. So the challenge now targets the other half of the pair.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him say (suggests stating only one thing)

phrases.english: Then let him say [only]: 'The halakha follows the lenient view in eruv.'

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: Why do I need 'The halakha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question around after Step 11: now the specific ruling looks extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the specific ruling 'הלכה כרבי יוחנן בן נורי'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule alone already produces the lenient ruling for the sleeping person, so the specific ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The specific ruling covers one opinion against many
steps.stepSummary: The specific ruling was needed. Without it, we might think the lenient rule works only between equal sides, not when a lone opinion opposes the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: that rule applies only when one authority disagrees with one, or many disagree with many. But when one authority stands against many, I would say it does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the specific ruling adds. It shows we follow the lenient view even when a single Sage is lenient against the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the הלכה follows the majority (יחיד ורבים הלכה כרבים). So one might think 'follow the lenient view in עירוב' covers only evenly matched disputes. Here רבי יוחנן בן נורי is one person against the חכמים, so the specific ruling teaches that the lenient rule overrides even the majority. Each ruling now has its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
One authority against many (a lone view against the majority)

steps.whatToRemember: Each ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches something new. The general rule ('follow the lenient view in עירוב') means we follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי only where he is lenient. The specific ruling shows the lenient rule applies even when one Sage stands against the majority.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule of following the lenient view in עירוב is strong enough to override the usual rule of following the majority.

phrases.english: It was necessary; it would have entered your mind to say
that this applies only [where] one [disputes] against one
or many against many,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יָחִיד בִּמְקוֹם רַבִּים — אֵימָא לָא.
phrases.english: but one against many, I would say [it does] not [apply].
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן בן נורי is a single Sage disputing the חכמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves Step 12 by showing what the specific ruling adds.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lenient rule might apply only between equal sides, not a lone view against the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: We follow the lenient view in עירוב even when a lone Sage is lenient against the majority.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rulings are needed: the general one limits us to leniencies, and the specific one extends the lenient rule to a lone view against the majority.

steps.title: רבא: In Rabbinic Law, Lone vs. Many Shouldn't Matter
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks אביי why we distinguish between יחיד במקום יחיד and יחיד במקום רבים, since עירובין is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to אביי: Since the laws of עירובין are rabbinic, what difference does it make to me whether it is one sage against one sage or one sage against many sages?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the answer from step 13. That answer said the specific ruling was needed because one sage disputing many is different from one sage disputing one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said the general lenient rule might cover only an even dispute (one vs. one). רבא argues that in a rabbinic area like עירובין we are lenient anyway, so the number of sages on each side should not matter. If so, the general rule alone would cover everything, and the problem of the 'extra' specific ruling comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since; introduces an assumed fact used to build an argument
Rabbinic in origin, not from the Torah
A lone opinion against another lone opinion (an even dispute)
A lone opinion against the majority

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not questioning the rule of being lenient in עירוב. He is questioning only the distinction between one-against-one and one-against-many.

phrases.english: Rava said to Abaye:
Now, since eiruvin are rabbinic,
what difference is it to me, a single sage against a single sage,
or a single sage against many!
phrases.notes: The 'מה לי... ומה לי' wording is a way of saying both cases should be treated the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְאַבָּיֵי: מִכְּדֵי עֵירוּבִין דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 13, which relied on the one-vs-many distinction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between יחיד במקום יחיד and יחיד במקום רבים used in step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a rabbinic area we are lenient regardless, so the majority-vs-minority distinction is irrelevant. The general rule would cover both cases, making the specific ruling unnecessary.

steps.title: רב פפא: Even in Rabbinic Law the Distinction Exists
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא: is there really no difference in rabbinic laws between one-vs-one and one-vs-many?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Do we really not distinguish, in rabbinic laws, between one sage against one sage and one sage against many?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back against רבא's claim. This line sets up the proof that comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said rabbinic status erases the difference between minority and majority disputes. רב פפא doubts this. He is about to show a rabbinic case where a lone opinion against the majority is clearly treated as weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes no difference to us

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
And in rabbinic laws is there no difference for us
between a single sage against a single sage
and a single sage against many?!
phrases.notes: Read as a rhetorical question: of course there is a difference!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: וּבִדְרַבָּנַן לָא שָׁנֵי לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's קשיא from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that in rabbinic matters the one-vs-many distinction does not matter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a known rabbinic case where a lone opinion against the majority is treated as weaker. So the distinction does exist even in דרבנן.

steps.title: The משנה: רבי אלעזר on a Woman Who Missed Three Cycles
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא cites a משנה where רבי אלעזר rules that a woman who passed three expected cycles is impure only from the time she sees blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה that רבי אלעזר says: any woman who has gone three expected periods without bleeding is impure only from the moment she sees blood, and not retroactively.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins his proof by quoting a משנה from the laws of נדה. This step sets up the case; the punchline comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the rabbis declare a woman impure retroactively, for up to a day (מעת לעת), when she finds blood. That retroactive impurity is a rabbinic rule. רבי אלעזר is lenient for any woman who missed three cycles. The חכמים limit this leniency to older women and similar cases, so רבי אלעזר is a lone opinion against the majority, in a rabbinic matter.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? Introduces a source used as a proof or challenge
It is enough for her from her time: she is impure only from the moment she sees blood, not retroactively

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna: Rabbi Elazar says:
Any woman over whom have passed
three expected cycles —
it is enough for her from her time (of seeing).
phrases.notes: She is not made impure retroactively.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the first half of the source behind רב פפא's challenge in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That even in rabbinic matters, a lone opinion against the majority is treated differently.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדה quoting רבי אלעזר, who stands alone against the חכמים in a rabbinic matter.

steps.title: רבי Relied on רבי אלעזר Only in a Pressing Situation
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא relates that רבי ruled like רבי אלעזר. When he remembered that רבי אלעזר was a lone opinion, he said he may be relied on only בשעת הדחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: Once רבי ruled in an actual case like רבי אלעזר. Afterward he remembered that the majority disagreed. He said: רבי אלעזר is worthy to rely on in a pressing situation.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of רב פפא's proof. רבי treats a lone opinion against the majority as usable only in an emergency, even though the matter is rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If minority-vs-majority did not matter in rabbinic law, רבי could rely on רבי אלעזר all the time. Instead he limited it to שעת הדחק. This shows that even in דרבנן, a lone opinion against many is weaker, which challenges רבא's claim in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident in which he acted (ruled in practice)
רבי יהודה הנשיא, compiler of the משנה
After he remembered (that it was a minority view)
In a pressing or emergency situation

steps.whatToRemember: Even in a rabbinic matter, רבי relied on a lone opinion against the majority only בשעת הדחק. This is רב פפא's proof that the difference between יחיד במקום יחיד and יחיד במקום רבים still matters in דרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a minority opinion may be relied on בשעת הדחק became a major principle in later פסק הלכה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי did not say his ruling was wrong. He said a minority view is good enough in a pressing case, but not as a standard ruling.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a baraita: It once happened that Rebbi ruled
in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.
After he remembered (that the majority disagree), he said:
Rabbi Elazar is worthy
to rely upon in a pressing situation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: מַעֲשֶׂה וְעָשָׂה רַבִּי כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 16 by showing how רבי treated רבי אלעזר's minority view.
steps.raayaObject: That in rabbinic matters, יחיד במקום רבים is still weaker than an even dispute.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי limits reliance on רבי אלעזר's lone view to שעת הדחק, even though retroactive נדה impurity is rabbinic.

steps.title: What did רבי suddenly remember?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'after he remembered' means in the ברייתא. It rejects the reading that רבי remembered the הלכה had been decided like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'after he remembered' mean? If you say he remembered that the הלכה is not like רבי אלעזר but like the רבנן, then how could he follow רבי אלעזר even בשעת הדחק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain one phrase in the ברייתא, 'after he remembered.' It tries one meaning and shows that it cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the הלכה had already been officially decided against רבי אלעזר, nobody could rely on him, not even in an emergency. Yet רבי still allowed relying on him בשעת הדחק. So what רבי remembered must have been something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading that is about to be rejected)
How could he act like him?

phrases.english: What does "after he remembered" mean?
If you say: after he remembered
that the halakha is not like Rabbi Elazar
but like the Rabbis
then how could he act like him even in a pressing situation!
phrases.notes: A ruling already decided against someone cannot be used even in an emergency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a key phrase in the ברייתא brought in step 17, so the proof can work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly did רבי remember that made him limit his ruling to בשעת הדחק?

steps.title: He remembered that רבי אלעזר stood alone against many
steps.stepSummary: No official הלכה had been decided. רבי remembered that many disagreed with רבי אלעזר, so he limited reliance on him to בשעת הדחק. This proves that one-against-many matters even in rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, no הלכה had been stated, neither like רבי אלעזר nor like the רבנן. 'After he remembered' means he remembered that not one person but many disagreed with רבי אלעזר. So he said: רבי אלעזר is worthy to rely on בשעת הדחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning: רבי remembered that רבי אלעזר was a lone voice against a majority. This finishes רב פפא's proof against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before he remembered, רבי ruled like רבי אלעזר freely. Once he realized it was one against many, he cut it down to emergencies only. The law of a נדה's retroactive impurity is rabbinic, so even in rabbinic matters one-against-one and one-against-many are treated differently.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי's ruling shows that even in a rabbinic law, a lone opinion against many is weaker. It can be relied on only בשעת הדחק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for relying on a minority opinion בשעת הדחק when no final הלכה has been decided.

phrases.english: Rather: the halakha had not been stated
neither like Rabbi Elazar nor like the Rabbis.
"After he remembered" that it was not one person disagreeing with him
but many who disagree with him,
he said: Rabbi Elazar is worthy
to rely on in a pressing situation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 and completes רב פפא's challenge to רבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי remembered that רבי אלעזר was a יחיד against רבים, while no official הלכה had been decided.
steps.raayaObject: Even in rabbinic laws there is a difference between יחיד במקום יחיד and יחיד במקום רבים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about רבי's ruling in the case of the woman who passed three expected cycles.

steps.title: A second challenge to רבא about rabbinic laws
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא, or some say רב נחמן בר יצחק, also asks רבא: is there truly no difference in rabbinic laws between one-against-one and one-against-many?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said to רבא, and some say it was רב נחמן בר יצחק who said to רבא: In rabbinic laws, is there no difference between one against one and one against many?
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage now challenges רבא's claim from step 14. This line sets up a new proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had said that since עירובין is only rabbinic, the size of the opposing group should not matter. This challenger holds that it does matter even in rabbinic laws, and he will bring a different source to show it.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a different version of who said it)

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said to Rava,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak who said to Rava:
And in rabbinic laws is there no difference
between one opinion against one opinion,
and one opinion against many?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לְרָבָא וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב פפא's challenge is completed, a second, parallel challenge to רבא's position begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim (step 14) that in rabbinic laws there is no need to distinguish יחיד במקום יחיד from יחיד במקום רבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rhetorical question implying that a source shows the distinction does apply in rabbinic laws. The source follows in the next step.

steps.title: The ברייתא about near and distant news of a death
steps.stepSummary: The challenger begins his proof with a ברייתא: a שמועה קרובה requires שבעה and שלשים, while a שמועה רחוקה requires only one day of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But was it not taught in a ברייתא: A near report (of a relative's death) requires שבעה and שלשים. A distant report requires only one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenger quotes a ברייתא about mourning to build his proof. This is setup: the גמרא will next show how this source proves the point about one-against-many.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שמועה קרובה is news heard within thirty days of the death. In that case the mourner keeps the full שבעה and שלשים. A שמועה רחוקה is news heard after thirty days, and then only one day of mourning is kept. Mourning beyond the first day is a rabbinic matter, so this is a fitting test case for רבא's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a challenging source)
A near report, news of a death heard within thirty days
A distant report, news of a death heard after thirty days
The seven-day and thirty-day mourning periods

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not finished here. This ברייתא is only the starting point. Steps 22-25 show the dispute and how the הלכה is decided about it.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
A near report: one practices seven and thirty days of mourning,
phrases.notes: News of the death arrives within thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: רְחוֹקָה אֵינָהּ נוֹהֶגֶת אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: a distant report: one practices only one day.
phrases.notes: News of the death arrives after thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא שְׁמוּעָה קְרוֹבָה נוֹהֶגֶת שִׁבְעָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge raised in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That even in rabbinic laws (mourning), the distinction between יחיד במקום יחיד and יחיד במקום רבים applies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on שמועה קרובה and שמועה רחוקה in the laws of אבלות. Steps 22-25 complete the proof.

steps.title: Defining a near report and a far report: רבי עקיבא against the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי עקיבא defines a near report as within thirty days and a far report as after thirty days. The חכמים say both kinds of report require שבעה and שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which report counts as near, and which counts as far? Within thirty days it is near. After thirty days it is far. These are the words of רבי עקיבא. The חכמים say: whether the report is near or far, the mourner keeps seven days and thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from step 21, which now explains what near and far mean. It also shows that this is a dispute between one sage, רבי עקיבא, and many sages, the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא is lenient: if the news comes after thirty days, the mourner keeps only one day. The חכמים are strict: the mourner always keeps the full שבעה and שלשים. This sets up a clear case of one lenient sage against many strict sages, which is exactly what the proof needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Near, meaning news of a death that arrives within thirty days
Far, meaning news of a death that arrives after thirty days

phrases.english: And which is considered near
and which is considered far?
Within thirty days, it is near;
after thirty days, it is far,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
But the Sages say:
Whether a near report
or a far report,
one observes seven and thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵי זוֹ הִיא קְרוֹבָה וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא רְחוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in step 21 and supplies the dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That one-against-many matters even in rabbinic law
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי עקיבא, a lone lenient view, against the strict חכמים

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like the lone רבי עקיבא as an exception
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן states a general rule: when one sage is lenient and many are strict, the הלכה follows the many. He makes an exception here and rules like רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: wherever one sage is lenient and many are strict, the הלכה follows the many who are strict. The exception is this case. Even though רבי עקיבא is lenient and the חכמים are strict, the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenger brings a ruling by רבי יוחנן on this dispute. He calls the case an exception to the usual majority rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mourning is a rabbinic matter. Even so, רבי יוחנן treats 'one lenient against many strict' as a normal reason to follow the many, and he says this case is a special exception. That suggests one-against-many matters even in rabbinic law, which challenges רבא's claim from step 14.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because רבי יוחנן had to call this an exception, the general rule must apply even in a rabbinic area. That is the heart of the proof.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Wherever you find
a single sage lenient and many strict,
the law follows the strict majority,
except for this case,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מֵיקֵל
phrases.english: where even though Rabbi Akiva is lenient
and the Sages are strict,
the law follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the dispute quoted in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That the majority rule applies even in rabbinic matters
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement that this case is an exception

steps.title: Why the exception: רבי יוחנן agrees with שמואל on mourning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן's exception comes from שמואל's rule. In mourning laws, the הלכה follows the lenient opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds like שמואל, because שמואל said: the הלכה follows whoever is lenient in mourning laws.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן broke his own majority rule here. The reason is a special rule for mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exception is not because rabbinic law ignores the majority. It is because mourning has its own rule: always follow the lenient view. This narrows the exception to mourning alone.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose rule is to follow the lenient view in mourning

phrases.english: And he holds like Shmuel,
for Shmuel said:
the law follows the lenient opinion in mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the exception in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In mourning laws, the הלכה follows the lenient view.

steps.title: Outside mourning, one-against-many matters even in rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: Only mourning is treated leniently. In all other areas, even rabbinic ones, there is a difference between one-against-one and one-against-many.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only in mourning that the רבנן were lenient. In general, even in rabbinic laws, there is a difference between one sage against one sage and one sage against many sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion of the proof. רבא's claim from step 14 is rejected: the number of sages does matter even in rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוחנן needed a special mourning rule to follow the lone רבי עקיבא, the majority rule must normally apply even in rabbinic law. This explains why רבי יהושע בן לוי had to say explicitly that the הלכה follows the lone רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatToRemember: Mourning is a special case where we follow the lenient view. Everywhere else, even in rabbinic law, a lone opinion against many is weaker than a lone opinion against one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This justifies רבי יהושע בן לוי's explicit ruling, which רבא had questioned.

phrases.english: It is in mourning that the Rabbis were lenient,
but in general,
even in rabbinic laws there is a difference
between one sage against one sage
and one sage against many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from steps 23 and 24. This completes the challenge of step 20 and rejects רבא's claim from step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Except in mourning, the difference between one-against-one and one-against-many applies even to rabbinic law.
